subject: Request for clarification: constraints in data block

messages.author: ebac19664dad3407
messages.subject: Request for clarification: constraints in data block
parts:
How should I think about constraints on variables declared in the data block?

I am reading chapter 6 of the manual, on time-series modeling, and note that in the MA(2) and MA(Q) models (Sect. 6.3, pp. 46-48), the dimension of the data vector is constrained:

data {
int<lower=3> T;
vector[T] y;
...
}

and
data {
int<lower=0> Q;
int<lower=3> T;
vector[T] y;

In section 3.2 on constrained data types the manual says that constraints are very significant on variables declared in the parameter block, but implies that in the data block they only provide an error check on the data at initialization.

I also notice that the manual is somewhat  loose in the constraints in the data block (e.g., often constraining the minimum length of data vectors to be zero, even though a minimum length of 1 would seem more strictly necessary; setting the minimum length of the data vector for an MA(Q) model to 3, when (Q+1) would seem to be necessary, etc.), whereas the manual emphasizes that it is important that constraints in the parameter block be strict in the sense of forbidding any values of parameters outside the domain of the model's support. This distinction reinforces my sense that data constraints don't really affect model performance.

But since I'm not certain about this I would like to ask for clarification: Are there optimizations or other performance-related things that make use of constraints in the data block (and similarly, in the transformed_data, transformed_parameters, and generated_quantities blocks) or are they strictly for error checking the input?

Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Request for clarification: constraints in data block
parts:
On Aug 7, 2014, at 5:25 PM, Jonathan Gilligan <jonathan...@gmail.com> wrote:

> How should I think about constraints on variables declared in the data block?
>
> I am reading chapter 6 of the manual, on time-series modeling, and note that in the MA(2) and MA(Q) models (Sect. 6.3, pp. 46-48), the dimension of the data vector is constrained:
>
> data {
> int<lower=3> T;
> vector[T] y;
> ...
> }
>
> and
> data {
> int<lower=0> Q;
> int<lower=3> T;
> vector[T] y;
>
> In section 3.2 on constrained data types the manual says that constraints are very significant on variables declared in the parameter block, but implies that in the data block they only provide an error check on the data at initialization.

For the parameters, they define transforms plus Jacobians that
define the space over which sampling is actually done. There the
constraints have to be at least as strict as the support of the model.

For the data block, it's just error checking.

Setting a minimum of T=3 in the MA(2) model makes sure there's at least
one data point. It technically could be T=2 without causing an error
because Stan's "for (t in 3:T)" does not behave like R's, so that if
T < 3, there are no loop iterations, rather than going backward from
3 down to T like R does.

> I also notice that the manual is somewhat loose in the constraints in the data block (e.g., often constraining the minimum length of data vectors to be zero, even though a minimum length of 1 would seem more strictly necessary; setting the minimum length of the data vector for an MA(Q) model to 3, when (Q+1) would seem to be necessary, etc.),

That was just sloppiness. I'll fix it in the next manual and
clarify the above.

> whereas the manual emphasizes that it is important that constraints in the parameter block be strict in the sense of forbidding any values of parameters outside the domain of the model's support. This distinction reinforces my sense that data constraints don't really affect model performance.
Correct --- it's just error checking that's evaluated once on data input.

> But since I'm not certain about this I would like to ask for clarification: Are there optimizations or other performance-related things that make use of constraints in the data block (and similarly, in the transformed_data, transformed_parameters, and generated_quantities blocks) or are they strictly for error checking the input?

No --- strictly for error checking.

- Bob
